second_look.name: Poltrona Eames, Up (1.18)
second_look.reason: Agree. Rear view with a clean 1 px ink, 3-tone copper ramp, 8 colours, foot gap 1, silhouette mirror difference 0.7%: it sits beside the best catalogue pieces and reads at 1:1 in the lit overview. Its outline has two inks, the navy frame (#30325e, 72 boundary px) and the dark-copper cushion (#623436, 14 px), 96.6% of the boundary together; the first second opinion's 81% counted the navy alone. The only defect is data, not art: its 27 solid rows are 18 px of real height, so the shadow is too long (caster h 18).

second_look.name: 14.2 Computador iMac (sobre móvel), front: monitor, keyboard, mouse (direction Down)
second_look.reason: Agree (46 placements, the fourth most repeated keep). A clean front elevation: screen, stand, keyboard and mouse, readable at 1:1 and the brightest thing on every desk of the lit overview. Nothing to change.

second_look.name: Cadeira de escritório giratória, Up (1.16)
second_look.reason: Agree with the audit's keep, after a correction. The first second opinion upgraded this to touch-up on '11% of the boundary is ink', which was an artifact of a one-ink measure (the darkest teal, 8 px). Drawn with one ink per material, as bake.py draws them, 77.8% of the boundary is in an ink (dark teal #0f262c and the navy #30325e of the armrests, wheels and base), measured by contract.py outline_share. The armrests are outlined on their outer sides, the rim of the backrest is a teal highlight with no ink, and the foot gap is 3 rows. Form, ramp and silhouette read at 1:1 beside the Eames. It stays a ratchet offender of outline (77.8% against 90%) and of foot_gap, so a redraw is held to the limit; the optional touch-up (ink the backrest rim) is cheap but not urgent. 46 placements (53 with the Down twin).

second_look.name: 3.10 Mesa de escritório (gavetas à esquerda)
second_look.reason: Agree for the art, with two caveats. At 1:1 in the lit overview the desk reads as a desk (white slab, drawer pedestal, one leg) under its monitor. The top is a single flat colour (mean run 11.7 against a catalogue median of 2.4), and the slab's light slate rim is drawn on row 0 of the canvas, which contract.py edge_touch flags (a rim in a lighter tone than the darkest ink cannot be told from a cut). Its outline is two inks, a light slate rim on the slab and a dark slate one under it, 97.8% of the boundary together (the first second opinion's 44% counted only the darker). And its 40 rows are 10 px of real front face (rows minus 30 px of footprint depth): the shadow is about 4 times too long, which is the visible defect: a caster entry fixes it with no new pixel.
